mix.bumpy_ride.note: Few things, big ups and downs

result.title: What 500 futures look like
result.loss: Futures that end below what you put in: {chance}.
insight.title: What this shows
insight.short_deadline: Your deadline is close. In your worst 1 in 20 futures you ended below what you put in. Money you need soon has little time to recover from a fall.
insight.all_bumpy: Most of your money is on the Bumpy Ride. The range is very wide. Much better and much worse outcomes are both possible, and no one can say which you get.
insight.steady_and_long: A steady mix swings very little. Over a long time, rising prices can eat into slow growth. Switch on the inflation adjustment to see it.
insight.loss_chance: In {loss} of these futures you ended below what you put in. Taking more risk makes the range wider in both directions.
insight.long_wait: A long wait lets good and bad years even out, and the middle of the range tends to rise. It never becomes a promise.
insight.default: No one can promise one number. Look at the whole range, not just the middle line.
open.hint: Test your plan against 500 possible futures.
paths.title: Meet the three paths
paths.intro: Each path is a made-up place to keep money. They differ in how much they grow and how much they swing. Splitting means choosing how many of every 100 rupees go to each one.
paths.steady_box.what: Like a savings box. Few surprises, but it grows slowly.
paths.mixed_basket.what: Like a basket of many small things. One bad item hurts less, but the basket still rises and falls.
paths.bumpy_ride.what: Like a few big bets. It can climb fast, and it can fall hard.
paths.year: In a typical year, ₹10,000 ends between {low} and {high}.
paths.note: A typical year means about 2 years out of 3. Some years fall outside it. These paths are made up for learning, not real products.
paths.learnRisk: Learn first: Risk, return and swings
p1.title: What are you saving for?
p1.hint: Pick one goal. The numbers are already filled in for you.
p2.title: Meet the three paths
p2.hint: Your money can sit in three made-up places. Read how they differ, then continue.
p3.title: Split your money
p3.hint: Decide how many of every 100 rupees go to each path. There is no right answer.
p4.title: What 500 futures look like
p4.hint: Each future is one way things could go. Look at the range, not one number.
